summary:
MissionCrafters is an interactive space mission design game for web and desktop. Players choose a lunar, Mars, or other mission, define success requirements, and build a spacecraft by selecting its components, instruments, orbit, and launch vehicle. They then simulate the mission and review flight events, resource use, and results.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex spacecraft design decisions easier to understand. Players see how changing mass, power, budget, science, communications, or schedule can affect mission success. They can adjust their design and try again, learning through experimentation rather than only reading about engineering concepts.

MissionCrafters includes NASA Planetary Data System references and NASA imagery search to add real mission context. Its guided tutorial, visual simulation, and mission reports help students connect classroom science with practical space exploration decisions. This matters because hands-on experimentation can make STEM concepts clearer and help learners understand the trade-offs behind real missions.
details:
Project Details

MissionCrafters is an educational space mission design game for web and desktop. It gives players a chance to plan a spacecraft mission, make engineering choices, simulate the flight, and learn from the outcome. The project is designed to make the interconnected decisions behind space missions easier to explore through hands-on experimentation.

What it does and how it works

Players begin by choosing a mission scenario and difficulty, then set requirements that define success. They design a spacecraft by choosing compatible parts, instruments, payloads, an orbit, and a launch vehicle. As they work, the interface shows how the design affects key resources, including mass, power, budget, data, communications, and time.

Once the design is ready, players run a mission simulation. A visual flight timeline shows mission events, while telemetry and resource indicators track the spacecraft’s performance. At the end, a report summarizes the outcome and score. Players can revise the design and run the mission again to see whether their changes improved the result.

The game also includes a guided tutorial and AutoBuild suggestions. AutoBuild can use the project’s local mission-aware builder, with optional AI-generated suggestions when the online service is available. NASA Planetary Data System references and NASA Images search add context to the missions and design process. The game uses curated dataset references and imagery metadata; it does not download raw archive measurements for the simulation.

Benefits and intended impact

Spacecraft design involves trade-offs. Adding instruments may improve science return but add mass and increase power needs. A different orbit may help coverage while affecting communications or mission duration. MissionCrafters makes these relationships visible and lets players experiment without needing to build a real spacecraft.

The intended impact is to help students connect classroom science and engineering concepts with the decisions involved in space exploration. Instead of only reading that engineering choices have consequences, players can change a design, simulate it, and observe the result. The tutorial, live design feedback, visuals, and reports are intended to support learning through exploration and iteration.

Tools and technologies

The web client is built with React, TypeScript, and Vite. The project includes a custom mission simulation and scoring engine, interactive spacecraft design screens, telemetry and flight visuals, and curated NASA dataset references. The desktop version uses Python and PyWebView to display the same web application in a native window.

Optional online features use Supabase for authentication, cloud blueprint and mission-progress storage, team rooms, and verified leaderboard submissions. A Supabase Edge Function can connect AutoBuild requests to the Gemini API; the Gemini key stays on the server and is not embedded in the app. The project can fall back to its local AutoBuild logic when the AI service is unavailable.

What makes it creative

MissionCrafters combines spacecraft design, resource management, mission simulation, and interactive learning in one experience. Players are not just selecting a winning answer: they make their own design, observe the consequences, and decide what to change. The same mission can invite different strategies, giving players room to test ideas and compare outcomes.

Factors considered

The project considers mission requirements, compatibility between spacecraft parts, and the effects of design choices on mass, power, budget, science, communications, and schedule. It also considers accessibility for learners: the tutorial introduces the workflow, visual indicators explain constraints while designing, and the report helps players understand what happened. NASA references are presented as mission context rather than as raw data driving a scientifically validated flight model. Online features are optional for the core design and simulation experience; cloud sync, online teams, and server-verified scores require an internet connection and account sign-in.
